editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the computational-basis explanation, measure_all's default ClassicalRegister, measure_active sizing, and the mid-circuit caveat. Nothing would mislead a learner. Two things are worth changing. First, 'measurement' as a noun is rendered 'sukat' ('ang mga sukat ay isinasagawa', 'Mag-apply ng sukat sa isang circuit'). Second, 'method' is rendered 'paraan ng X' ('Gamitin ang paraan ng measure'), which reads as 'the way of measure' and clashes with 'paraan' meaning 'way' in entry [9]. editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The removal notes, the deprecation caveats and the v1.x support dates all match the source. editor_note: The translation is faithful on the parts that carry the argument: the even and odd parity reasoning, the two categories of closed loops, distance L, [[2L^2,2,L]] and the 10% threshold caveat. editor_note: The translation is faithful overall. Core terms stay consistent throughout: qubit, ansatz, orbital rotation, configuration recovery, "may laman / walang laman" for occupied and empty, and "pagtatantya" for estimation. A few spots need a fix. In [40], "every other orbital" became "Ang bawat iba pang orbital", which reads as "each of the other orbitals" rather than alternating orbitals; the 0th/2nd/4th examples right after it rescue the meaning. In [74], "only" was dropped from "configurations with only correct particle numbers". [97] has an ungrammatical "tinatayang ang ground state energy" and uses "sumasaklaw" (covers) where "occupy" was meant. editor_note: Overall the meaning is faithful: the horizontal/vertical line reasoning, the CNOT pairs (0-1, 1-2, 2-3, then 4-5, 5-6, 6-7), the 60% and 100% accuracies and the barren-plateau caveat all come through, and the key terms are consistent. examples.source: Sometimes, quantum computers are compared to giant, exponentially-scaling parallel processors. But this isn't quite right. While a piece of the answer...
examples.translation: Ngunit hindi ito tama. Kahit ang bahagi ng sagot sa tanong na ito ay nasa tinatawag na "quantum parallelism,"
examples.suggested: Ngunit hindi ito lubos na tama. Bagaman ang bahagi ng sagot sa tanong na ito ay nasa tinatawag na "quantum parallelism,"
examples.why: The source hedges ('not quite right'), and the translation turns it into a flat rejection. 'Kahit' also reads as 'even' rather than the concessive 'while/although'.

examples.source: how the community's thinking on quantum computing has evolved over time
examples.translation: kung paano naging-iba ang pag-iisip ng komunidad
examples.suggested: kung paano nagbago ang pag-iisip ng komunidad
examples.why: 'naging-iba' is not a well-formed verb; 'nagbago' or 'nag-iba' is natural.

examples.source: used the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm to solve a more specific, restricted problem
examples.translation: para malutas ng isang mas tiyak at limitadong problema
examples.suggested: para malutas ang isang mas tiyak at limitadong problema
examples.why: Wrong case marker ('ng' for the object/focus 'ang'). The same slip appears in [121] ('malutas ng kanilang problema').

examples.source: the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm will return the string $s$
examples.translation: ibibalik ng Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm ang string $s$
examples.suggested: ibabalik ng Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm ang string $s$
examples.why: Typo in the future-aspect reduplication.

examples.source: for the sake of this problem, we think of this function as a "black box."
examples.translation: para sa layunin ng problemang ito, inaakalang ito ay isang "black box."
examples.suggested: para sa layunin ng problemang ito, itinuturing natin itong isang "black box."
examples.why: 'inaakala' suggests a presumption, often a mistaken one. The English means a deliberate modelling choice, which 'itinuturing' conveys.

examples.source: harness superposition, entanglement, and interference
examples.translation: ang superposisyon, entanglement, at interference
examples.suggested: ang superposition, entanglement, at interference
examples.why: Superposition is kept in English in [18], [36] and [41] ('superposition state') but becomes 'superposisyon' here and in [100] and [131]. The file should pick one form.

editor_note: The teleportation protocol, the outcome/correction table and the faster-than-light reasoning all keep the English meaning, so nothing here would mislead a learner. A few sentences still need fixing. In [109], "we will not name a single qubit A" became "hindi na namin magpapalitan ng pangalan", which means "we won't swap names". In [95], "exhausted your free monthly use" uses the wrong verb "naagahan" where it should be "naubos". Measurement is split between "sukat" (early entries) and "pagsukat" (later ones), and collapse is split between "mag-collapse" and "pagguho" ([131], [136]). Smaller slips: [85] drops "only" ("This is only done for us to check ourselves"), [66] has "talagang ilipat mo ito" in the wrong tense, and calques like "Sa lahat ng paraan" for "By all means" and "May malakas na kagustuhan" for "strong preference" read stiffly.

examples.source: So we will not name a single qubit "A" and another "B".
examples.translation: Kaya hindi na namin magpapalitan ng pangalan sa isang qubit na "A" at isa pa bilang "B".
examples.suggested: Kaya hindi natin papangalanan ang isang partikular na qubit na "A" at ang isa pa na "B".
examples.why: 'magpapalitan ng pangalan' means 'exchange/swap names', not 'assign a name'; in a section about swap gates this muddles the point that A/B are no longer fixed qubits.

examples.source: But in case you have exhausted your free monthly use
examples.translation: Ngunit kung naagahan mo na ang iyong libreng buwanang paggamit
examples.suggested: Ngunit kung naubos mo na ang iyong libreng buwanang paggamit
examples.why: 'naagahan' is the wrong verb (it relates to being early/ahead of time); 'exhausted' here means 'naubos'.

examples.source: the collapse of a quantum state propagates faster than light
examples.translation: ang pagguho ng isang quantum state ay kumakalat nang mas mabilis
examples.suggested: ang collapse ng isang quantum state ay kumakalat nang mas mabilis
examples.why: Earlier the page uses 'collapse'/'mag-collapse' ([11], [23], [25]). Switching to the literal 'pagguho' (crumbling) in the quiz breaks consistency with the concept students were taught.

examples.source: This is only done for us to check ourselves.
examples.translation: Ito ay ginagawa natin para masuri ang ating sarili.
examples.suggested: Ginagawa lang natin ito para masuri ang ating sarili.
examples.why: Dropping 'only' weakens the point that the inverse-U step is a verification trick and not part of teleportation.

examples.source: But it can be moved, and indeed you will move it in this module.
examples.translation: Ngunit maaari itong ilipat, at talagang ilipat mo ito sa module na ito.
examples.suggested: Ngunit maaari itong ilipat, at talagang ililipat mo ito sa module na ito.
examples.why: The bare 'ilipat' reads as a command or as incomplete; the future tense 'ililipat' is needed.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The meaning stays faithful throughout, including the static-MPF "HINDI nakadepende" negation, the k_j=19 comparison, and the caveat about the approximate model. Several word choices are calques or plain wrong words. In [67], "tight convergence criteria" is rendered "masisigasig" ("diligent"). In [40], "satisfy t/k_min < 1" becomes "masiyahan sa" (pleased by), and in [33] "coefficients of interest" becomes "coefficient na interesado". In [52], "constrains the L1-norm to a chosen threshold" is softened to "nagpapaliit" (shrinks). Smaller slips are "nag-yi-yield" in [43] and "ila-laktawan" in [62].

examples.source: the importance of using tight convergence criteria
examples.translation: ang kahalagahan ng paggamit ng masisigasig na convergence criteria
examples.suggested: ang kahalagahan ng paggamit ng mahigpit na convergence criteria
examples.why: 'masisigasig' means diligent or zealous. A tight criterion is 'mahigpit'.

examples.source: normally tells us to satisfy $t/k_{\text{min}} \lt 1$
examples.translation: karaniwang nagsasabi sa atin na masiyahan sa $t/k_{\text{min}} \lt 1$
examples.suggested: karaniwang nagsasabi sa atin na dapat matugunan ang $t/k_{\text{min}} \lt 1$
examples.why: 'masiyahan' means to feel satisfied or pleased. It is a calque of the English word, not the mathematical sense of meeting a condition.

examples.source: which constrains the L1-norm to a chosen threshold while minimizing the difference of $Ax$ and $b$
examples.translation: na nagpapaliit sa L1-norm sa napiling threshold habang minimi-minimize ang pagkakaiba ng $Ax$ at $b$
examples.suggested: na naglilimita sa L1-norm sa loob ng napiling threshold habang mini-minimize ang pagkakaiba ng $Ax$ at $b$
examples.why: 'nagpapaliit' (shrinks) blurs the difference between the constraint (an upper bound) and the objective being minimized.

examples.source: where $x$ are our coefficients of interest
examples.translation: kung saan ang $x$ ay ang ating mga coefficient na interesado
examples.suggested: kung saan ang $x$ ay ang mga coefficient na hinahanap natin
examples.why: This literally says the coefficients are the ones who are interested. It is a calque of 'of interest'.

examples.source: a second-order Suzuki-Trotter formula yielding `order=2`
examples.translation: second-order Suzuki-Trotter formula na nag-yi-yield ng `order=2`
examples.suggested: second-order Suzuki-Trotter formula, kaya `order=2`
examples.why: 'nag-yi-yield' is awkward code-switching. A native writer would restructure the sentence.

editor_note: In entry [37], 'scale' is translated as 'sumusukat', which means 'measures'. The sentence now says the circuits or sampling overhead 'measure in a way that is not depth-efficient', so the reason these algorithms need fault-tolerant hardware (their cost grows poorly with problem size) is lost, and a learner could misunderstand it. The other problems are minor. In [6], 'advantage ... over a classical computer' uses a bare 'sa' where 'kumpara sa' or 'laban sa' is clearer. In [72], 'sa halaga ng pagtaas' is a word-for-word copy of 'at the cost of'; natural Tagalog is 'kapalit ng'. In [14], 'nag-encode' uses the completed aspect for a general present-tense statement. Tutorial link titles are translated inconsistently: some are rendered in Tagalog, most are left in English, and [77]/[78] lowercase 'circuit cutting' at the start of the title.

examples.source: The circuits or sampling overhead for these algorithms scale in a manner that is not depth-efficient
examples.translation: Ang mga circuit o sampling overhead para sa mga algorithm na ito ay sumusukat sa paraang hindi depth-efficient
examples.suggested: Ang mga circuit o sampling overhead ng mga algorithm na ito ay lumalaki (nag-i-scale) sa paraang hindi depth-efficient
examples.why: 'sumusukat' means 'measures', not 'scales'. The point about how cost grows, which is why these algorithms wait for fault-tolerant hardware, gets lost.

examples.source: at the cost of increased classical compute overhead
examples.translation: sa halaga ng pagtaas ng classical compute overhead
examples.suggested: kapalit ng mas malaking classical compute overhead
examples.why: This copies the English idiom 'at the cost of' word for word; 'kapalit ng' is the natural way to say a trade-off in Tagalog.

examples.source: computational advantage by a quantum computer over a classical computer
examples.translation: computational advantage ng quantum computer sa isang classical computer
examples.suggested: computational advantage ng quantum computer kumpara sa classical computer
examples.why: A bare 'sa' does not clearly express the comparison 'over'. 'kumpara sa' makes the comparison explicit.

examples.source: whose output distributions encode solutions
examples.translation: na ang output distribution ay nag-encode ng mga solusyon
examples.suggested: na ang output distribution ay nag-e-encode ng mga solusyon
examples.why: 'nag-encode' is the completed aspect, but this is a general present-tense statement, so it needs the ongoing aspect 'nag-e-encode'.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The critical angle (~0.3π), the noise pushing it right toward 0.5π, the 21×12 circuit count and the torino/pittsburgh qubit counts all match the English. The worst slip is "sweep", rendered as "sumasalakay"/"sinasalakay" ("attacks/invades") in [45] and [47]. It's the wrong word, but the 21-values context keeps it from teaching a false idea. Smaller problems: "relies on" became "inaaasahang gamitin" ("expected to use", also misspelled) in [10]; "restricted" became "pinaghigpit" (a calque) in [25] and [36]; "peak near +N and −N" became "nakasentro" ("centered") in [58]; and "pushed all the way" became the stiff "inilipat nang lahat-lahat" in [74].

examples.source: which by default sweeps across 21 values
examples.translation: na bilang default ay sumasalakay sa 21 values
examples.suggested: na bilang default ay dumaraan sa 21 value (sweep)
examples.why: 'sumasalakay' means 'attacks/invades', not 'sweeps'. It's the wrong word for a parameter sweep, and [47] repeats it as 'sinasalakay'.

examples.source: the section on mid-circuit measurement that the GEM protocol relies on
examples.translation: ang seksyon sa mid-circuit measurement na inaaasahang gamitin ng GEM protocol
examples.suggested: ang seksyon sa mid-circuit measurement na pinagbabatayan ng GEM protocol
examples.why: 'relies on' became 'expected to use', which weakens a hard dependency. 'inaaasahang' is also a typo.

examples.source: the distribution would still peak near +N and -N
examples.translation: ang distribusyon ay nakasentro pa rin malapit sa $+N$ at $-N$
examples.suggested: ang distribusyon ay may tuktok pa rin malapit sa $+N$ at $-N$
examples.why: 'Centered' is imprecise for a bimodal distribution. The English says it has peaks near both values.

examples.source: The plaquette lattice is restricted to a single plaquette
examples.translation: Ang plaquette lattice ay pinaghigpit sa isang plaquette lamang
examples.suggested: Ang plaquette lattice ay nililimitahan sa isang plaquette lamang
examples.why: 'pinaghigpit' ('tightened') is a calque of 'restricted'. 'nililimitahan' is the natural word here. The same calque appears in [36] and [47].

examples.source: the peak has been pushed all the way to $0.5 \pi$
examples.translation: ang peak ay inilipat nang lahat-lahat hanggang sa $0.5 \pi$
examples.suggested: ang peak ay naitulak hanggang sa mismong $0.5 \pi$
examples.why: 'nang lahat-lahat' is a stiff, unnatural rendering of 'all the way'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The key claims all survive intact: the variational upper bound, noise costing subspace quality rather than correctness, M_J imposed on recombined products rather than whole shots, and the identical support of qubit and fermionic excitations. A few word choices still need a native editor's fix. "fitted to measured spectra" became "naaangkop" (which means "applicable"). "vanishing matrix element" became "nawawala" (which means "missing"). "might not detect" was strengthened to "hindi maaaring matukoy" ("cannot be detected"). "ranked" became "inayos", which clashes with "ayusin" used elsewhere in the file for "repair". There are also small slips: the ungrammatical "maliit pa rin sapat" in [40], a plural/formal "inyong" in [110], and dropped intensifiers ("far larger", "well above").

examples.source: an empirical two-body force fitted to measured spectra
examples.translation: isang empirical two-body force na naaangkop sa sinukat na spectra
examples.suggested: isang empirical two-body force na in-fit sa mga sinukat na spectra
examples.why: 'naaangkop' means 'applicable/appropriate', not 'fitted'. It hides the idea that the interaction's parameters are fitted to data, and entry 165 correctly uses 'in-fit'.

examples.source: can reveal recoupling errors that a single energy calculation might not detect
examples.translation: mga recoupling error na hindi maaaring matukoy ng isang solong energy calculation
examples.suggested: mga recoupling error na maaaring hindi matukoy ng isang solong energy calculation
examples.why: The English hedge 'might not detect' became 'cannot be detected', which overstates the claim.

examples.source: have a vanishing matrix element
examples.translation: ay may nawawalang matrix element
examples.suggested: ay may matrix element na zero (naglalaho)
examples.why: 'nawawala' reads as 'missing/lost', not 'equal to zero'.

examples.source: every ranked excitation
examples.translation: bawat inayos na excitation
examples.suggested: bawat naka-rank na excitation
examples.why: 'inayos' can mean 'repaired', and the file uses 'ayusin' for the repair step. Entry 134 uses 'naka-rank', so this rendering is also inconsistent.

examples.source: the first is still small enough to diagonalize exactly on a laptop
examples.translation: ang una ay maliit pa rin sapat upang i-diagonalize nang eksakto
examples.suggested: sapat pa ring maliit ang una para ma-diagonalize nang eksakto
examples.why: 'maliit pa rin sapat' is ungrammatical because it copies English word order (calque).

examples.source: to evaluate your results
examples.translation: para suriin ang inyong mga resulta
examples.suggested: para suriin ang iyong mga resulta
examples.why: 'inyong' is a plural/formal slip. The rest of the file uses the casual 'iyong/mo'.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, including the difficult caveats. The long diagonal-filter passage [59] correctly says the filter changes the evolved operator and the qDRIFT bounds, while the classical diagonalization stays variational. The pruning trade-off [91] and the L1-norm and step-angle explanation [26] are also correct. The problems are naturalness and consistency. In [16], "gamit ang isang ensemble" comes right after "kukuha ng sample ng bitstrings", so the "replace the ansatz with an ensemble" structure is hard to see. Some phrasings are calques or awkward: "nagpapakain sa interference" (feed into), "Habang" used for concessive "While", "nadedepine/Magdedepine", and the tense slip "nag-sample" for the habitual "samples". "Term" also switches between "term" ([20], [23], [28]) and "termino" ([48] onward).

examples.source: replaces the need to choose an ansatz from which to sample bitstrings with an ensemble of time-evolution circuits
examples.translation: pumapalit sa pangangailangang pumili ng ansatz kung saan kukuha ng sample ng bitstrings gamit ang isang ensemble ng time-evolution circuits
examples.suggested: sa halip na pumili ng ansatz na pagkukunan ng sample ng bitstrings, gumagamit ito ng ensemble ng time-evolution circuits na direktang binuo mula sa target Hamiltonian
examples.why: The placement of 'gamit ang' makes it read as if the bitstrings are sampled using the ensemble, which hides that the ensemble is what replaces the ansatz.

examples.source: those relative phases feed into the interference generated by the excitation terms
examples.translation: ang mga relative phase na iyon ay nagpapakain sa interference
examples.suggested: ang mga relative phase na iyon ay nakakaapekto sa interference
examples.why: 'Nagpapakain' is a literal calque of 'feed into' and sounds odd in technical Tagalog.

examples.source: While it increases the dimension of the subspace we want to diagonalize, the workflow still gives us an accurate answer
examples.translation: Habang pinapataas nito ang dimension ng subspace ...
examples.suggested: Bagama't pinapataas nito ang dimension ng subspace ...
examples.why: 'Habang' means 'while' in the time sense. This sentence needs the concessive 'bagama't'.

examples.source: the QDriftTrotterization pass that we will use in the future samples random indices
examples.translation: ay nag-sample ng random indices
examples.suggested: ay nagsa-sample ng random indices
examples.why: The completed-aspect form 'nag-sample' does not fit a habitual or future action.

examples.source: Term grouping
examples.translation: Pagpapangkat ng termino (Term grouping)
examples.suggested: Use 'termino' consistently (entries 20/23/28 use 'term')
examples.why: 'Term' is rendered as both 'term' and 'termino' in the same file.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The Step 4 heading [52] was left completely in English. A few phrasings are stiff or slightly off. "along the edges" became "kasama ng mga edges" [39], which reads as "together with the edges". "align more closely" became "mas malapitan" [7]; "malapitan" means close-range, and it should be "mas malapit". The completed-aspect "tumantiya" is used where an ongoing relative clause "tumatantiya" is needed [33, 40]. The survey line also slips into formal "Mangyaring" [58], which breaks the casual register.

examples.source: Step 4: Post-process and return result in desired classical format
examples.translation: Step 4: Post-process and return result in desired classical format
examples.suggested: Step 4: I-post-process at ibalik ang resulta sa nais na classical format
examples.why: This is the only step heading left untranslated, while Steps 1-3 are in Tagalog.

examples.source: implemented with layers of `RZZ` gates along the edges of the interaction graph
examples.translation: ipinatupad gamit ang mga layer ng `RZZ` gates kasama ng mga edges ng interaction graph
examples.suggested: ipinatupad gamit ang mga layer ng `RZZ` gates sa bawat edge ng interaction graph
examples.why: "kasama ng" means "together with", not "along/on". It blurs the point that each RZZ gate acts on one graph edge.

examples.source: the hardware results align more closely with noiseless simulations
examples.translation: ang mga resulta ng hardware ay mas malapitan sa noiseless simulations
examples.suggested: ang mga resulta ng hardware ay mas lumalapit sa noiseless simulations
examples.why: "malapitan" means close-range or up close. It is the wrong word for "agree more closely".

examples.source: we construct circuits that approximate the time evolution operator
examples.translation: bubuo tayo ng mga circuits na tumantiya sa time evolution operator
examples.suggested: bubuo tayo ng mga circuit na tumatantiya sa time evolution operator
examples.why: The completed aspect "tumantiya" is ungrammatical for a general property. The same slip appears in [40].

examples.source: Please take a minute to provide feedback on this tutorial.
examples.translation: Mangyaring maglaan ng isang minuto upang magbigay ng feedback sa tutorial na ito.
examples.suggested: Maglaan ng isang minuto para magbigay ng feedback sa tutorial na ito.
examples.why: "Mangyaring" is formal, which conflicts with the casual register convention.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The criteria, T1 decay, GHZ scaling and the Toffoli decomposition all hold up, and nothing would mislead a learner. A native editor would still fix several literal calques. 'on the fly' became the meaningless 'sa fly' in [33]. 'touched on' became 'hinawakan' ([77]), which means physically touched. 'on the order of' became 'sa order ng' ([78]). 'By the end' became 'Sa wakas' ([12]), which means 'finally'. There are also small slips. [40] names the agent twice ('Awtomatiko nitong i-aaplay ng simulator'). [34] says 'iba't ibang panimulang state' ('various') where the English means 'a different one'. [68] has 'sa Bob' where it should be 'kay Bob'. [12] spells 'intuwisyon' and [79] spells 'intuisyon'.

examples.source: reinitialize a qubit to |0〉 on the fly
examples.translation: muling i-initialize ang isang qubit sa |0〉 sa fly
examples.suggested: muling i-initialize ang isang qubit sa |0〉 habang tumatakbo ang circuit
examples.why: This is a literal calque of an English idiom. 'sa fly' means nothing in Tagalog.

examples.source: we also touched on quantum communication aspects
examples.translation: hinawakan din natin ang quantum communication aspects
examples.suggested: bahagya rin nating tinalakay ang quantum communication aspects
examples.why: 'hinawakan' means physically touched or held. It does not mean 'discussed briefly'.

examples.source: By the end, you'll have a deeper intuition
examples.translation: Sa wakas, magkakaroon ka ng mas malalim na intuwisyon
examples.suggested: Sa dulo ng notebook, magkakaroon ka ng mas malalim na intuwisyon
examples.why: 'Sa wakas' means 'finally, at last'. That drops the idea of 'by the end of this notebook'.

examples.source: The simulator will automatically apply the T1/T2 errors
examples.translation: Awtomatiko nitong i-aaplay ng simulator ang T1/T2 errors
examples.suggested: Awtomatikong i-aaplay ng simulator ang T1/T2 errors
examples.why: The agent is named twice ('nito' and 'ng simulator'), which is ungrammatical.

examples.source: If you needed a different starting state
examples.translation: Kung kailangan mo ng iba't ibang panimulang state
examples.suggested: Kung kailangan mo ng ibang panimulang state
examples.why: 'iba't ibang' means 'various/multiple'. The source means a single different state.
